title: Bounded seek and read behavior
statement: Let $Q,T,S$ be types with decidable equality, let $M$ be a Boolean multi-tape machine with $k$ work tapes, let $\operatorname{upd}:T\times\operatorname{Option}(\mathrm{Bool})\to T$, and let $\mathrm{seek}$ be a two-work-tape Boolean machine with designated states $\mathrm{start},\mathrm{finish}$ and a natural-number bound constant $C$. For every Boolean input $x$, configuration $c$ of $M$ on $x$, and Boolean word $w$, suppose that from every two-tape configuration $a$ on input $x$ in state $\mathrm{start}$ whose first tape stores $w$ around its head at offsets $-1$ through $|w|$ and whose second tape is blank, there is a time $t\le C(|w|+a_{\mathrm{in}}+c_{\mathrm{in}}+1)$ at which $\mathrm{seek}$ first reaches $\mathrm{finish}$; through time $t$ both work-tape heads stay within distance $C(|w|+1)$ of their initial positions, and at time $t$ the input-head position equals that of $c$, while both tapes, both work-head positions, and the output are unchanged. Suppose also that $d$ is a four-tape configuration over record symbols on the digit-embedded input, tape 2 is blank, and $\mathrm{saved}$ is a record-symbol list with $\mathrm{data}$ record data. Then there is a time $t\le C(|w|+d_{\mathrm{in}}+c_{\mathrm{in}}+1)+3$ such that the record-step machine reaches the specified snapshot in the seek phase from the specified seek-start snapshot, does not reach either verdict phase earlier, and keeps every work-tape head within distance $C(|w|+1)$ of its initial position throughout.
